questions.q: When is a conflict resolution policy actually relevant in Cosmos DB?
options: Only in multi-region-write (multi-master) mode, where more than one region can accept writes to the same item
In every Cosmos DB account, regardless of write mode
Only when using the Core (SQL) API
Only when the account has a single region configured
questions.explain: Conflicts require more than one writer at once, which is only possible when multi-region writes are enabled — single-region write mode has exactly one writer.

questions.q: How does the default Last-Writer-Wins (LWW) policy pick a winner between conflicting writes?
options: It keeps the version with the higher value on a designated property, by default the system timestamp
It always keeps the write that arrived at the primary region first
It merges both conflicting writes together automatically
It rejects both writes and requires manual resubmission
questions.explain: LWW compares a designated property (defaulting to the system timestamp) and keeps the higher value; the other write is discarded.

questions.q: Why might a team point LWW's conflictResolutionPath at their own application-maintained counter instead of the default system timestamp?
options: Clock skew across regions can make wall-clock 'last' ambiguous; a monotonic application counter is a more reliable tiebreaker
The system timestamp is always inaccurate and unusable
Cosmos DB requires a custom path in every configuration
It has no effect on how conflicts are resolved
questions.explain: The lesson explains this exact reasoning — an app-maintained version counter avoids ambiguity from cross-region clock skew.

questions.q: When should a team use custom conflict resolution (a stored procedure) instead of Last-Writer-Wins?
options: When silently discarding the losing write is unacceptable, such as with a shopping cart or a ledger entry that needs to be merged, not dropped
Whenever the account is in single-region-write mode
Custom resolution should always be used instead of LWW in every scenario
Only when using the Cassandra API
questions.explain: LWW is fine for data where losing a write is acceptable; data needing a real merge (like cart contents) needs custom resolution logic instead.

questions.q: What does 'manual' conflict resolution mode do?
options: Writes conflicting versions to a conflicts feed for the application to read and resolve on its own schedule
Automatically merges all conflicts using machine learning
Blocks all writes until a human manually approves each one in the Azure portal
Deletes both conflicting versions permanently
questions.explain: Manual mode defers resolution entirely to the application, which reads unresolved conflicts from the conflicts feed.
